title: signal.schema.json has no links array; cross-signal relationships are encoded as non-extensible ad-hoc top-level fields
description:
signal.schema.json encodes cross-signal relationships as individual top-level string fields: superseded_by is the only one. As the signal lifecycle becomes richer — a1000087 proposes fixed_by, validated_by, validates; a1000088 proposes forwarded_to — each new relationship type requires a new top-level field in both the schema and the Rust struct. This is not extensible and creates divergence between what the schema permits and what is written.

The problem is compounded by a1000087, which refers to 'the existing links array' as the target for its proposed link types. No links array exists in signal.schema.json or the Rust signal struct. Any signal file written with links: [] today is schema-invalid and the Rust deserialiser would drop it silently. a1000088 compounds this by proposing forwarded_to as a top-level field rather than a link entry, repeating the same mistake.

Signals written during the session on 2026-06-10 (Ariadne acknowledged signals) added forwarded_to and acknowledged_on as top-level fields in Ariadne signal files — both are schema-invalid and use the wrong pattern. Those fields must be migrated to links entries once this signal is resolved.

The correct pattern is a typed links array where each entry has a discriminating 'type' field and type-specific additional properties — analogous to GitHub linked_issues, JIRA issue_links, and git commit trailers.
proposed_resolution:
1. Add a links property to signal.schema.json:
   {
     "links": {
       "type": "array",
       "default": [],
       "items": {
         "type": "object",
         "required": ["type"],
         "properties": { "type": { "type": "string" } },
         "additionalProperties": true
       }
     }
   }

2. Add the corresponding Rust types: struct SignalLink { link_type: String, #[serde(flatten)] props: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> } and update SignalRecord to include links: Vec<SignalLink> defaulting to empty.

3. Deprecate superseded_by as a top-level field. Add a migration: when reading a signal with a top-level superseded_by string, surface it as a { type: 'superseded_by', signal_id: <value> } link entry. Keep the top-level field writable for one release cycle, then remove it from the schema. Update the status description for 'superseded' to reference the links array instead.

4. Establish the canonical link type vocabulary (implementations follow in gated signals):
   - superseded_by: { type, signal_id } — this signal is replaced by the referenced signal
   - forwarded_to: { type, signal_id, timestamp } — forwarded to the owning project's catalogue; timestamp = when forwarded (a1000088)
   - fixed_by: { type, run_id, candidate_tag, branch } — a run produced a prospective fix for this signal (a1000087)
   - validated_by: { type, signal_id } — a validation signal was created to verify the fix (a1000087)
   - validates: { type, signal_id, validation_type } — this signal validates the referenced signal (a1000087)

5. Update accept_signal, archive_signal, and the fix_signal and run skill files to write link entries rather than top-level fields for superseded_by and any future relationship types.

6. After resolution: migrate the 5 Ariadne acknowledged signals (3a7f9e1b, 6b8c0d2e, 9c0e1f2a, f2a3b4c5, a1b2c3d4) from top-level forwarded_to/acknowledged_on fields to correctly structured links entries.
